Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of mistreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Local Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Local Government cooperates with government agencies, other local governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, the Local Government as well as the participation of the business sector and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of mistreatment and neglect. 12. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Local Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Local Government cooperates with government agencies, other local governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, the Local Government as well as the participation of the business sector and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, so as to cause anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children victims of mistreatment and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, so as to cause anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Local Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Local Government cooperates with government agencies, other local governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, the Local Government as well as the participation of the business sector and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 19
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of job opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an Agreement.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 20
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and standards for fulfillment;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 8
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d are those who, as a matter of law, have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as members of the family.

Article 16
Letter a
What is meant by the right to have one’s dignity respected is upholding human rights.

Letter b
Sufficiently clear.

Letter c
Sufficiently clear.

Letter d
What is meant by the right to obtain information is the right to obtain explanations, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts, or their explanations, which can be seen, heard, and read, presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology, either electronically or non-electronically, related to acts of violence.

Letter e
Sufficiently clear.

Letter f
What is meant by the victim’s right to social rehabilitation includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.

Letter g
What is meant by the right to compensation includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health guarantees, and education or skills.

Letter h
What is meant by the right to the handling of complaints is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.

Letter i
Sufficiently clear.

Letter j
What is meant by the right to assistance includes, among others, psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members.

What is meant by an assistant is an individual who works as a volunteer to provide protection and support to women and children who are victims of acts of violence during the judicial process; assistants can come from family members, friends, or independent organizations that give attention to victims, as well as advocates.

Article 15
(1) The Regional Government, in the context of providing protection services to women and children victims of violence, establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center.
(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children victims of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of violence, abduction, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, entrapment, debt, or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of the person holding control over that person or another person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes: prostitution; forced labor or service; slavery or practices similar to slavery; oppression; extortion; physical exploitation; sexual exploitation; exploitation of reproductive organs; or unlawfully transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and/or body tissue; or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits, both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e Sufficiently clear.

Article 3
The regulation of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

Article 23
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be adjusted to the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER X
FINANCING
Article 22
Budget allocation for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Other lawful sources of income in accordance with Laws and Regulations; and
c. Other sources of income that are non-binding in nature.

CHAPTER III
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 5
Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children victims of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community;
c. Family; and
d. Parents.

CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
Article 12
Regional Governments are obligated to provide complaint service units for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 21
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

Article 24

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and mistreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any action/behavior/sexual gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, so as to cause anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.

CHAPTER X
FINANCING
Article 22
Budget allocation for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Other lawful sources of income in accordance with Laws and Regulations; and
c. Other sources of income that are non-binding in nature.

Article 23
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be adjusted to the regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

I. GENERAL
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Local Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Local Government cooperates with government agencies, other local governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, the Local Government as well as the participation of the business sector and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 19
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of job opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an Agreement.
